body.purpose: All primary reading text. Hard 16sp floor for purchase-critical content.

shadows.name: resting-card
shadows.purpose: Near-invisible lift on product cards (1dp); tonal color does the real separation.

shadows.name: floating-bar
shadows.purpose: Sticky checkout/cart bars floating over scrolling content (8dp). The only pronounced shadow.

motion.name: state-standard
motion.purpose: Material 3 standard easing for state transitions; motion conveys state, never decoration.

narrative.overview: A calm, curated shop — not a marketplace. Few products per view, imagery leads, and the shelf never shouts. A light-only, green-tinted world where hierarchy comes from type weight and tonal surfaces, never from noise. Every screen behaves like a well-kept storefront: the goods are the color, the chrome recedes, and money is the one thing the interface is never casual about.
keyCharacteristics: Light-only theme on a green-tinted near-white (mist), designed for bright ambient light
Restrained color strategy: brand green ≤10% of any screen, on actions and selection only
Gold appears exclusively at money moments — wallet, deposits, cashback, discounts
One type family (Roboto), weight-driven hierarchy, 16sp body floor
Depth is tonal; shadows are earned by floating surfaces only

rules.name: The Gold-Means-Money Rule
rules.body: Ledger Gold is forbidden anywhere money is not being shown. If gold appears on screen, the user is looking at rupees. No decorative gold, ever.

rules.name: The Quiet Shelf Rule
rules.body: Brand green covers at most ~10% of any screen. It marks the action and the selection; everything else is neutral.

rules.name: The 16sp Floor Rule
rules.body: Anything the user must read to complete a purchase renders at ≥16sp. All sizes in sp; layouts must survive 1.3× system font scale.

rules.name: The Earned Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow above 1dp requires the surface to float over other content. Static cards never get bigger shadows to pop; step the container tone instead.

dos: Do reserve Ledger Gold exclusively for money: wallet, deposits, cashback, discounts.
Do keep brand green to the action and the selection — ≤10% of any screen.
Do label every rupee on screen: product price vs. deposit vs. wallet credit vs. cashback.
Do use skeleton blocks for loading, teaching empty states, and fix-naming error states on every screen.
Do keep all text in sp, body ≥16sp, touch targets ≥48dp, and verify 4.5:1 contrast.
Do use standard Material 3 controls; earned familiarity over novelty.
donts: Don't build cold-marketplace density — badge clutter, cramped listings, promo noise.
Don't use urgency mechanics: countdown timers, "only 2 left!", flashing promos.
Don't add eco-cliché decoration: leaf icons, kraft textures, greenwashing copy.
Don't put gold on anything that isn't money, or use color as the only signal.
Don't give resting cards shadows above 1dp, nest cards, or invent non-standard controls.
Don't introduce a second type family or a dark theme.
